value="<b><font style="font-size: 12px;">How it Works</font></b><div><div><strong data-start="145" data-end="174" style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193)); font-size: 12px;">Route 1 — Direct Accounts</strong><div><div><span style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">Required lowest-level Account Planning Keys are defined in the controlled schedule and used as the driving table for the transaction join. This limits the resulting dataset to only the financial profiles required by the modeller.</span></div><div><strong data-start="408" data-end="440" style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">Route 2 — Calculated Members</strong></div><div><span style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">Calculated members are mapped to their underlying Account Planning Keys in the same controlled schedule. Transactions are joined to these mappings, then aggregated back to the parent member to derive metrics such as Gross Margin.</span></div><div><strong data-start="674" data-end="694" style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">Why this matters</strong></div><div><span style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">Account scope and calculation definitions remain outside the transformation code. Users can extend the controlled schedules without changing the underlying Power Query logic.</span></div></div></div></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="288.47" width="485" x="257.5" y="694.5" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="48" edge="1" parent="2" source="47" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;innerLoopWaypoints=1;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;" target="47"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

Transparent derivation: calculated metrics are built from explicit, inspectable rules

div.span: Required lowest-level Account Planning Keys are defined in the controlled schedule and used as the driving table for the transaction join. This limits the resulting dataset to only the financial profiles required by the modeller.

strong.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

span.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

div.span: Calculated members are mapped to their underlying Account Planning Keys in the same controlled schedule. Transactions are joined to these mappings, then aggregated back to the parent member to derive metrics such as Gross Margin.

strong.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

span.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

div.span: Account scope and calculation definitions remain outside the transformation code. Users can extend the controlled schedules without changing the underlying Power Query logic.
